title: iDecide: Development and Evaluation of a Digital Single-Session Decision Aid to Reduce Decisional Conflict About Internet Use: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial
summary:
Gaming and internet use can enrich everyday life, but they can also be associated with negative consequences. As a result, some people may feel uncertain about whether and how they would like to change their usage habits. This study aims to investigate whether the online decision aid iDecide is more effective in reducing this uncertainty than an online information resource about internet use.

We aim to recruit 50 adults who are considering changing their internet use but have not yet made a decision. At the beginning of the study, participants complete an online questionnaire and take part in a telephone interview about their internet use. They are then randomly assigned to one of two online programs.

The decision aid iDecide uses established psychotherapeutic techniques to help participants reflect on their internet use, clarify their personal goals, and weigh potential next steps. The alternative program provides information about internet use and includes a knowledge quiz. Both programs take approximately 30 to 45 minutes to complete.

Participants complete additional online questionnaires immediately after completing their assigned program and again four weeks after randomization.
conditions: Decisional uncertainty among adults considering a change in their gaming or other internet use. A diagnosis of gaming disorder or another internet-use disorder is not required for inclusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient proficiency in German.

- Access to an internet-enabled device and an internet connection.

- The individual is currently considering a change in their gaming and/or other internet use and has yet to make a final decision. This is operationalized as a score of 1 to 9 on the Readiness Ruler (0–10).

- Voluntary written or electronic informed consent after receiving study information.

A diagnosis of gaming disorder or another internet-use disorder and a minimum level of symptom severity are not required for inclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
- Current treatment or placement on a waiting list for treatment for gaming disorder or another internet-use disorder.

- Meeting or exceeding at least one of the following substance use screening cutoffs: Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test – Consumption (AUDIT-C) ≥ 4 for men or ≥ 3 for women, Cannabis Use Disorders Identification Test – Revised (CUDIT-R) ≥ 12, or Drug Use Disorders Identification Test (DUDIT) ≥ 25. This criterion does not apply to tobacco use.

- Self-reported current or past psychosis, bipolar disorder, or dissociative symptoms.

- Indications of acute suicidality at screening, operationalized as a score of 1 or higher on item 9 of the Beck Depression Inventory–II (BDI-II).
